More than 30 years after joining Dow Inc. as an intern, Karen Carter became the CEO this year, taking the helm of a company grappling with financial losses, a corporate restructuring, thousands of layoffs, and the shuttering of some European plants.
Not that she hadn't signed up for it. Carter took over the CEO role July 1 after helping create and implement the "transform to outperform" strategy announced in January.
"There's a saying that it's a blessing to be stressed by the thing you prayed for and hoped for," Carter told _Fortune_ . "This is really a privilege and an honor to be leading this company in such a time of change."
That change includes Carter representing both the first woman and the first Black CEO for the nearly 130-year-old manufacturer, which is the largest chemicals company in the Americas. Last week, as Carter presided over her first earnings report as CEO, she delivered more change.
